M-3.1-1: planned as 'normalisation returns the raw key'; committed as 'normalises to NFD instead of NFC' — the raw-key form left the unicodedata import unused (a lint-visible, not a behavioural, difference); the NFD form is a defect of the same requirement with the same target assertion

M-4.3-2: planned as 'the line is written before the conflict is raised'; not committed — moving the write is not a one-line change, and the 'no line appended' half of R-4.3 is measured by A-4.3-a's line count under M-4.3-1

A-3.3-f: assertion added beyond the plan: a removed middle line (A-3.3-e) is caught by the hash recomputation alone, so the prev_hash-equals-previous-hash rule of R-3.3 needed its own observation (a changed prev_hash field); without it M-3.3-2 was equivalent under the suite and would have been rejected

requirement_map.heading: Purpose
requirement_map.reason: purpose statement; the behaviours it names are R-3..R-9

requirement_map.heading: Non-Goals
requirement_map.reason: non-goals; the absence of network, server, UI and database is the shape of the reference, not a measured behaviour (R-12 measures the side-channel half)

requirement_map.heading: Key normalization (Unicode NFC)
requirement_map.behaviour: every key is NFC before storage, lookup, hashing and serialisation; NFD and NFC spellings are one key

requirement_map.heading: JSONL hash chain
requirement_map.behaviour: one JSONL line per mutation with hash = SHA-256(prev_hash || '|' || canonical bytes with hash and prev_hash blank); the first prev_hash is the literal GENESIS; lines are appended, never rewritten
requirement_map.interpretation: canonical bytes = JSON with sorted keys, no whitespace, non-ASCII kept; the constant is the literal string GENESIS

requirement_map.heading: Tamper evidence
requirement_map.behaviour: a full recomputation from disk detects a mutated value, a swapped op, a modified hash and a broken link, reporting the first bad index; a clean chain is ok

requirement_map.heading: Independent verify
requirement_map.behaviour: verify reads the chain from disk and consults nothing the instance remembers, so a tamper after the same instance appended is detected

requirement_map.heading: Request IDs
requirement_map.behaviour: a rid is a non-empty string; an empty rid is refused (ValueError; CLI exit 2) and nothing is written

requirement_map.heading: Idempotency
requirement_map.behaviour: a replayed rid returns the same result and appends nothing
requirement_map.interpretation: a rid is replayed when any committed line carries it, whatever its op or key

requirement_map.heading: Conflict
requirement_map.behaviour: a different rid on a key whose last committed mutation used another rid raises ConflictError (CLI exit 4) and appends nothing

requirement_map.heading: Tombstones
requirement_map.behaviour: a delete is a tombstone line; a put with a different rid conflicts against it; a put with the tombstone's rid is a no-op returning the delete's result; the key is absent from the snapshot

requirement_map.heading: Key-with-different-rid-different-op semantics
requirement_map.behaviour: put with r1 then delete with r2 conflicts; replays of the committed put do not conflict

requirement_map.heading: Atomic Batch Mutation
requirement_map.behaviour: a batch is planned against the chain and itself, then written as a whole through a sibling temp file, fsync and rename: all lines or none; a conflict anywhere commits nothing; a replay inside the batch appends once
requirement_map.interpretation: the CLI batch file is a JSON list of {op, key, value, rid, ts}; 'under the lock' is single-process serialisation (no threading module is allowed by R-10); a crash cannot be injected from outside, so atomicity is measured by its observable postconditions (bytes unchanged on refusal, old bytes a prefix on success, no temp sibling left)

requirement_map.heading: Deterministic Snapshot
requirement_map.behaviour: the snapshot holds the latest committed put per key unless tombstoned, keys sorted in UTF-8 byte order, byte-stable across calls; the CLI writes the same bytes

requirement_map.heading: Repair-tail
requirement_map.behaviour: a truncated final line is removed and the chain verifies afterwards; a clean chain is a no-op; corruption not confined to the tail is refused with the file untouched
requirement_map.interpretation: truncated = the final line is unterminated and does not parse or hash; a complete last line that fails its hash is corruption, refused

requirement_map.heading: Durability
requirement_map.behaviour: every function that opens the ledger for writing flushes and fsyncs before it returns
requirement_map.interpretation: durability cannot be observed from outside the process; the assertion reads the source of the tree

requirement_map.heading: CLI Exit Codes (exact contract)
requirement_map.behaviour: exit 0 on success, 2 on a usage error, 3 on an I/O error, 4 on a conflict, 5 on corruption (verify not ok, repair-tail refusal)

requirement_map.heading: Language / Runtime
requirement_map.behaviour: imports only the allowed standard-library modules; ledger.py and cli.py start with `from __future__ import annotations`
requirement_map.interpretation: the negative witness is a used import of a module outside the allowed set (M-10-1, two inserted lines: the import and its use)

requirement_map.heading: Tests and Coverage
requirement_map.reason: unit tests, 85% coverage and runner agreement are requirements on the product's own test suite; ProductProof never depends on developer tests (invariant IX) and this fixture measures product behaviour only; the mapping of test-named criteria is the DECISION-3 domain

requirement_map.heading: No Side Channels
requirement_map.behaviour: no socket, no subprocess, no os.system in the tree; the only files touched are the ledger, the batch input and the snapshot output
requirement_map.interpretation: the negative witness is an os.system call in the write path (M-12-1); the file-access half is a property of the reference's design (its opens name only those paths) and has no separate mutant

requirement_map.heading: Repository layout
requirement_map.behaviour: the package has __init__.py, ledger.py (Ledger, ConflictError, append, verify, snapshot, apply_batch) and cli.py; the imported package resolves inside the tree under evaluation
requirement_map.interpretation: the negative witness for the layout half is M-13-1 (ledger.py no longer defines apply_batch; the package re-exports a renamed function under that name); the in-tree resolution half cannot be violated by a product tree under python -I isolation and is witnessed by a harness calibration (the harness importing another tree is rejected by A-13-a). __main__.py is added so that `python -m ledgerlock` (R-9) runs; tests/, docs/, README and pyproject are the product repository's concern, not the reference's

requirement_map.heading: Acceptance
requirement_map.reason: items 1-4 and 6 are measured by the assertions named; item 5 (coverage) is R-11

mutant_catalog.consequence: keys are normalised to NFD instead of NFC: the spellings still meet, but the stored and snapshotted key is not the NFC form the requirement fixes; every snapshot keyed by an NFC non-ASCII key shows the NFD form
every hash is computed without the '|' separator; the chain is self-consistent but not the specified one, so only an independent recomputation sees it

mutant_catalog.before: prev = records[-1]["hash"] if records else GENESIS
mutant_catalog.consequence: append never chains: every line's prev_hash is GENESIS; verify (which recomputes linkage) rejects any chain of two or more appended lines, so every observation that verifies a multi-line chain or repairs one sees it

verify never recomputes a hash: a mutated value, op or hash field passes; corruption anywhere in a well-linked chain is invisible, so repair-tail no longer refuses mid-chain corruption and the CLI never exits 5 for it

verify never checks that prev_hash equals the previous line's hash: a changed prev_hash field goes unnoticed (a removed line is still caught by the hash recomputation, whose input is the previous line's hash)
first_bad_index is one too high; repair-tail, which compares it with the last index, refuses a genuinely truncated tail

mutant_catalog.after: return verify_raw(raw) if self._known_length is None else Verdict(True, None, self._known_length)
mutant_catalog.consequence: after this instance appended, verify answers from what it remembers instead of the disk

mutant_catalog.before: if not isinstance(rid, str) or rid == "":
mutant_catalog.consequence: an empty rid is accepted and a line is written with it

mutant_catalog.after: if rid in seen and seen[rid][1]["key"] != key:
mutant_catalog.consequence: a replayed rid on the same key is treated as new and appends again; every replay-based no-op (tombstone replay, NFC replay, in-batch replay, replay after a refused delete) appends instead

mutant_catalog.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutant_catalog.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] == rid:
mutant_catalog.consequence: the conflict condition is inverted and can never hold after the replay check, so no mutation conflicts: tombstones and different-op mutations are accepted, batches with a conflict commit, and the CLI never exits 4

mutant_catalog.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutant_catalog.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid and last_rec["op"] == "put":
mutant_catalog.consequence: only a live value conflicts; a tombstone no longer blocks a different rid

mutant_catalog.before: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid:
mutant_catalog.after: if last_rec is not None and last_rec["id"] != rid and last_rec["op"] == op:
mutant_catalog.consequence: a different rid conflicts only when it repeats the last op: delete-after-put and put-after-tombstone with a different rid are accepted

mutant_catalog.before: raise ConflictError(f"batch op {len(results)}: key {normalize_key(key)!r} was last mutated by another rid")
mutant_catalog.consequence: a conflict inside a batch ends the batch instead of refusing it: the ops before the conflict are committed (a partial batch) and the CLI exits 0
a rid first seen inside the batch is not remembered, so its replay later in the same batch appends a second line
the snapshot lists keys in insertion order, not UTF-8 byte order
a tombstoned key stays in the snapshot; every snapshot that must exclude a deleted key shows it
the clean-chain no-op never applies: repair-tail on an intact chain removes its last line
repair-tail no longer requires the first violation to be the last line: an unterminated file with mid-chain corruption is 'repaired' by dropping its tail instead of refused
repair-tail removes two lines instead of the truncated one
an append returns before its bytes are durable: no fsync in the append path
a conflict exits 5 instead of 4; every CLI observation of a conflict sees the wrong code
an I/O error exits 1 instead of 3

mutant_catalog.before: return EXIT_OK if verdict.ok else EXIT_CORRUPT
mutant_catalog.consequence: verify exits 0 whatever the verdict (the verdict on stdout is still correct)

changes.before: self._known_length = None   # what this instance last wrote; informative only, never a verdict's input
after: self._known_length = None   # what this instance last wrote; informative only, never a verdict's input
self._opened_at = time.time()   # a convenience field: when this instance was opened

mutant_catalog.multi_line_rationale: a disallowed module that is actually used needs its import statement and its use; joining them on one line with a semicolon would be an artificial one-line form, so the mutation is two inserted lines
mutant_catalog.consequence: ledger.py imports `time`, a module outside the allowed standard-library set of R-10, to stamp when a Ledger instance was opened; behaviour is otherwise unchanged
the atomic write shells out through os.system to flush the disks before the rename: a forbidden side channel (R-12: no os.system); the ledger's bytes are unchanged

changes.before: ConflictError, CorruptionError, Ledger, Result, Verdict, append, apply_batch, snapshot, verify,
changes.after: ConflictError, CorruptionError, Ledger, Result, Verdict, append, batch_apply as apply_batch, snapshot, verify,

mutant_catalog.multi_line_rationale: renaming the required definition alone would break the package import and turn every observation red for an import error, hiding the layout defect; re-exporting the renamed function under the required name keeps the tree runnable so the acceptance sees exactly the violation: ledger.py no longer defines apply_batch
mutant_catalog.consequence: ledger.py no longer defines the required name apply_batch (it defines batch_apply); the package hides it by re-exporting the new name as apply_batch, so nothing else observes the change
